pr_body:
Realized that when calculating if we should flush we weren't accounting for bytes pending in the writer (Advance hasn't been called on the PipeWriter yet). This could result in excess buffering and larger buffers being allocated (rented). Added test coverage for this scenario too.

Also fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/102532

review_comments: That sounds like we should add PipeWriter support to Utf8JsonWriter as well right?
What do you suggest that wouldn't be a breaking change?
We can do it outside of this PR btw. The discussion is good but we should have a dedicated issue (including the fact that it is a breaking change and what we want to do to mitigate it).

Absolutely, not in scope for this PR.

One possibility is we expose an additional constructor accepting `PipeWriter` that forces a different modality for `UnflushedBytes` so that users explicitly opt into that. Might be challenging to achieve that given that there already is one for IBufferWriter though.
Nit: Why not just add the `Utf8JsonWriter` to `WriteStack` along with the `PipeWriter`? It seems conceptually similar and it's always available when setting `WriteStack.PipeWriter`.
I believe it's echoing old convention in which async converter methods are overloads accepting `ref WriteStack` as an additional parameter.
